```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A's demand evidence is stronger. It cites three independent practitioner threads (dev.to, r/SaaS, r/Backend), each describing a concrete production incident or customer impact. B has only two quotes, and one of them is a secondhand anecdote on what appears to be a vendor's own blog.",
    "B faces an incumbent setting a $0 anchor. Slack Code is bundled free into every Slack plan, backed by Salesforce's distribution. A's free competitors are indie, beta, or open-source projects, and apidrift.co charges $29/mo, a paid anchor A could plausibly match.",
    "A's two load-bearing feasibility claims are not unsourced in its own brief. B's are: it marks both solo six-week buildability and demand from sales, support, and analyst teams as [unsourced], so both count as missing. That leaves B with only engineering demand and no evidence a solo build is feasible.",
    "A's job (watch → diff → scan → PR) is well-bounded and suits agent automation. Its GitHub Marketplace listing gives a sourced path to billing without a sales team, which fits a 90-day target for a first paying customer.",
    "B's brief concedes that SOC2, Zero Data Retention, SSO, and approval gating are plausibly the real purchase drivers. It also flags security review as a likely obligation before enterprise adoption. Both raise the bar for a solo operator to land a first paying team.",
    "Both ideas are crowded, with five or more competitors each, so neither wins on novelty. A has fewer structural blockers between it and one paying customer."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's lead demand quote (\"What did the agents actually produce last week?\") is a secondhand anecdote about an unnamed operations lead. It is hosted on agentcenter.cloud, which appears to be a company selling agent-visibility tooling, so it is likely self-interested marketing content rather than independent buyer pain. B's other strong-sounding demand signal, the YC Fall 2026 RFS, has no citation at all.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Neither brief shows direct willingness-to-pay evidence beyond competitor price lists. A carries real risks the briefs cannot resolve: three competitors are free, the brief reports that mendapi's own published studies found raw spec diffs over-report by about 8x, and granting PR access to source code is a trust hurdle. A's channel CAC figure also comes from a source flagged for a prompt-injection attempt, so I gave it no weight. A wins mainly because B faces a free incumbent bundle and its brief leaves its key feasibility claims unsourced."
}
```
